message.content:
**Best months to visit Hawaii:**  
- **April – May** (spring)  
- **September – October** (early fall)

### Why those months are ideal

| Month | Avg. High (°F / °C) | Avg. Low (°F / °C) | Rainfall (in / mm) | Crowds | Price level |
|-------|---------------------|--------------------|--------------------|--------|-------------|
| **April** | ~84 °F / 29 °C | ~68 °F / 20 °C | 0.5–1.0 in / 12–25 mm | Moderate | Medium |
| **May** | ~86 °F / 30 °C | ~70 °F / 21 °C | 0.4–0.8 in / 10–20 mm | Moderate | Medium |
| **September** | ~85 °F / 29 °C | ~69 °F / 20 °C | 0.3–0.7 in / 8–18 mm | Low‑to‑moderate | Low‑medium |
| **October** | ~83 °F / 28 °C | ~67 °F / 19 °C | 0.4–0.9 in / 10–23 mm | Low | Low |

*Sources:* NOAA climate normals for Honolulu (average over 30 years).  

### What to expect

- **Weather:** Warm, sunny days with comfortable evenings; humidity is lower than in summer.  
- **Rainfall:** Lowest in September and October; April and May still have occasional showers but are generally dry.  
- **Crowds & Prices:** These shoulder seasons see fewer tourists than the peak summer (June–August) and holiday periods (December–January), so you’ll find better deals on accommodations and shorter lines at popular attractions.  

### Bottom line

If you’re looking for a balance between pleasant weather, lower crowds, and reasonable prices, aim for **late spring (April–May)** or **early fall (September–October)**. If you don’t mind paying a bit more for the convenience of peak season, July and August offer the most consistent sunshine and are great for beach activities.
